{{Short description|Local ring in algebraic geometry}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''normally flat ring''' along a proper ideal <math>I</math> is a [[local ring]] <math>A</math> such that <math>I^n/I^{n+1}</math> is [[flat module|flat]] over <math>A/I</math> for all <math>n \geq 0</math>.

The notion was introduced by [[Heisuke Hironaka|Hironaka]] in his proof of the [[resolution of singularities]] as a refinement of [[equimultiplicity]] and was later generalized by [[Alexander Grothendieck|Grothendieck]] and others.
